items.title: LY4257496 Study for GRPR-Positive Advanced Cancers Including Prostate
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is testing a new drug called LY4257496 for cancers with high levels of a protein called GRPR, including prostate cancer. The study will evaluate safety and effectiveness both alone and combined with standard treatments. Participation lasts up to 36 weeks or until tumor progression.

items.title: BPX-601 CAR T-Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study will test BPX-601, a CAR-T cell therapy made from a patient's own immune cells, for advanced treatment-resistant prostate cancer that has spread. The study aims to determine safe dosing, potential side effects, and how well it destroys cancer cells. The trial is not yet recruiting patients.

items.title: AMG 509 Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates AMG 509 safety, tolerability, and early effectiveness in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The drug is being tested alone and in combination with standard treatments abiraterone and enzalutamide. Multiple study parts are currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, alone or with other treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine safe dosing, assess tolerability, and measure PSA response. Patients are currently being recruited.

items.title: TRC003 for PSMA-Positive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study evaluates TRC003, a PSMA-targeted therapy, in patients with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have already received hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The study will test three different doses in 90 patients over up to 6 treatment cycles.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) with chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is to determine if patients receiving I-DXd live longer overall and have longer progression-free survival than those receiving standard chemotherapy. This is a pivotal trial currently recruiting.

items.title: TD001 PSMA-Targeted Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study evaluates TD001, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting PSMA, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will assess safety, drug levels in the body, and preliminary anti-tumor activity. Patients are currently being recruited.

items.title: AZD2265 Phase 3 Trial Versus Standard Care in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares AZD2265 with standard treatments in PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to show AZD2265 improves radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. This is a pivotal trial currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Radiation Therapy for Recurrent or Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies side effects of shorter-course radiation therapy (proton beam or IMRT) for prostate cancer that has returned or spread to a limited number of sites after initial treatment. The study aims to determine if fewer, larger radiation doses can be as effective with potentially fewer side effects.

items.title: Olaparib With or Without Cediranib in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial compares olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone versus olaparib combined with cediranib in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. PARP inhibitors prevent cancer cells from repairing DNA damage, potentially stopping tumor growth. The trial is no longer recruiting new patients.

items.title: INR731 With or Without Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study evaluates INR731, a novel oral drug, alone or combined with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors in metastatic prostate cancer. The study will assess safety, tolerability, drug levels, and preliminary anti-tumor activity to determine the recommended dose for future studies.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 Trial in mCSPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat (an investigational drug) combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who haven't received prior hormone therapy. The study aims to determine if the combination works better than enzalutamide alone.

items.title: PDS01ADC With Docetaxel and Abiraterone in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests PDS01ADC (an antibody-drug conjugate) combined with docetaxel chemotherapy and/or abiraterone in both metastatic castration-sensitive and castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will evaluate safety and effectiveness of these combination approaches to delay disease progression.

items.title: Opevesostat Phase 3 Trial After Prior Hormone Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 study compares opevesostat plus hormone replacement therapy versus switching to alternative hormone therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after disease progression on one prior hormone agent. The study measures progression-free survival as the primary outcome.

items.title: AAA817 After Lu-PSMA Therapy Progression in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2/3 study evaluates AAA817 versus standard care in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose disease has progressed after Lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy. Patients must have previously received hormone therapy and chemotherapy. The study is recruiting patients.

items.title: Nivolumab, Docetaxel, and Hormone Therapy in mHSPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial combines nivolumab immunotherapy with docetaxel chemotherapy and androgen deprivation therapy for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients with DNA repair defects or inflamed tumors. The study tests whether adding immunotherapy to standard treatment improves outcomes in selected patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy Versus Observation in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares lutetium-177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto) radioligand therapy versus observation alone in oligometastatic prostate cancer that has recurred after initial treatment. The study aims to control disease progression early and delay the need for hormone therapy while preserving quality of life.

items.title: Clinical Review: Optimizing Care in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: This educational review provides a framework for managing metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in the modern treatment era. It discusses how to integrate clinical features, molecular testing, imaging, and supportive care to guide treatment decisions, given the complexity of sequencing multiple therapy options including hormone agents, chemotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and radioisotopes.

items.title: PKD1 Modulates PARP Inhibitor Sensitivity in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This laboratory study found that Protein Kinase D1 (PKD1) influences how well prostate cancer cells respond to the PARP inhibitor olaparib. Understanding these molecular interactions could help identify which patients are more likely to benefit from PARP inhibitors and potentially enable combination strategies that enhance effectiveness while reducing side effects.

items.title: Review: Novel Therapies Beyond Hormone Blockade in mCRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive review discusses new treatment strategies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer beyond standard hormone therapy. It covers PARP inhibitors for DNA repair defects, PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, immunotherapy approaches, and the role of liquid biopsies and PSMA-PET imaging in guiding treatment decisions and patient selection.

items.title: Review: Combination Strategies to Overcome PARP Inhibitor Resistance
items.summary: This review examines why PARP inhibitors eventually stop working and explores rational combination therapies to overcome resistance in prostate, ovarian, and breast cancers. Despite success in DNA repair-deficient cancers, most patients develop resistance over time, limiting long-term benefits. The review discusses emerging combination approaches to expand the patient population that can benefit.

items.title: Sirtuin1 Identified as Driver of Aggressive Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This genetic screening study identified Sirtuin1 (SIRT1) as a key driver of neuroendocrine prostate cancer, an aggressive variant that often develops after hormone therapy. Using mouse models and genetic analysis, researchers found that SIRT1 promotes features of this lethal cancer type and may represent a new therapeutic target.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in mCRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed a new drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks two cancer-driving pathways: BRD4 and AKT. This dual inhibitor overcomes resistance to AKT inhibitors that commonly develops through elevated c-MYC in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Laboratory studies showed promising anti-tumor activity.

items.title: RIPK2 Activity Signature Developed for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed a gene signature to measure RIPK2 activity in prostate cancer, which may help identify patients who could benefit from RIPK2-targeted therapies. The signature responded predictably to RIPK2 inhibition in laboratory studies and correlated with clinical outcomes in patient samples, potentially serving as a biomarker for future trials.

items.title: Review: Gut Microbiome and Drug Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review examines how gut bacteria and their metabolites may contribute to drug resistance in advanced prostate cancer treatment. Understanding the microbiome's role in treatment response could lead to novel strategies using probiotics, dietary interventions, or microbiome-targeted therapies to overcome resistance and improve outcomes.

items.title: L-MYC Drives Neuroendocrine Transformation in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study discovered that the L-MYC gene is selectively activated in neuroendocrine prostate cancer, an aggressive treatment-resistant form that can develop after hormone therapy. L-MYC drives the transformation to this lethal cancer type by suppressing androgen receptor signaling and activating neuroendocrine programs, representing a potential therapeutic target.
